'''Araogawa Shrine''' (荒雄川神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ōsaki, Miyagi|en|Ōsaki, Miyagi|qid=Q385892|lt=Ōsaki City}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|en|Miyagi Prefecture|qid=Q47896|lt=Miyagi Prefecture}}, Japan. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} was Gōsha. It is one of the three shrines in {{ill|Tamatsukuri District, Miyagi|en|Tamatsukuri District, Miyagi|qid=Q7680960|lt=Tamatsukuri District}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. The name "Araogawa" is another term for the {{ill|Eai River|ja|江合川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eai River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11550788}}.
== Deities ==
* The main deities are {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Sēoritsuhime no Mikoto|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sēoritsuhime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu-hime|qq=}}.
*** According to the {{ill|Jinjachō|ja|宮城県神社庁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyagi Prefecture Shrine Association|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社庁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590703}}, the primary deity is {{ill|Ōmonoimi no Kami|ja|大物忌神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi no Kami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3270544}}. However, shrine history and discussions with the chief priest suggest that Ōmononushi is not enshrined at Satomiya.
* Additional deities enshrined in auxiliary shrines include:
** {{ill|Mountain Shrine|ja|山神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yama Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11470798}} (deity: {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花咲耶姫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1781862}}) 
** {{ill|Tenjinsha|ja|天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11443279}} (deity: {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}})
** {{nihongo|'''Mikumari-sha'''|水分神}} (deity: {{ill|Mikuma-no-Kami|ja|水分神|1=Mikumari|2=ja|3=水分神|4=zh|5=水分神|6=sv|7=Mikumari-no-Kami|8=fr|9=Mikumari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikuma-no-Kami|qq=}})
== History ==
According to the shrine’s history, it was founded in {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō 4}} (720). It is one of the three {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} shrines in Tamatsukuri District. Araogawa Shrine in {{ill|Naruko Onsen|ja|鳴子温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruko Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11675321}}, another {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}}, serves as a counterpart to this one. The Iwadeyama Ikeduki shrine is referred to as "Satomiya" (lower shrine), while the Naruko Onsen shrine is "Takemiya" (upper shrine), with different priestly families managing each.
The main deities of Satomiya are Susanoo no Mikoto and Sēoritsuhime no Mikoto. Sēoritsuhime, known for purifying defilements, is worshipped as a water deity controlling the upper reaches of Araogawa. The reverence for the name "Ōmononushi no Kami" likely stems from the association with the river's pure flow and the prohibition against polluting the waters.
The shrine grounds have long been sacred, featuring Jōmon-period ritual sites known as the Araogawa Shrine Ruins. Artifacts like pottery and tools have been excavated. During the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Zenkunen War}}, the military governor {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} offered prayers and treasures, such as golden blades. In the {{ill|Gosannen War|en|Gosannen War|qid=Q1187411|lt=Gōsanen War}}, General {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} also prayed for victory.
In {{ill|Kaō (era)|en|Kaō (era)|qid=Q1150842|lt=Kaō 2}} (1170), {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidehira|en|Fujiwara no Hidehira|qid=Q3090625|lt=Fujiwara no Hidehira}} designated Araogawa Shrine as "Oshū’s First Shrine." The shrine received strong support from {{ill|Ōsaki clan|ja|大崎氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsaki氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2975417}}, the regional lords during the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi Period}}. During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}}, the shrine became the guardian shrine for the {{ill|Iwatesan Date Clan|ja|岩出山伊達家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwatesan Date Clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30922189}}.
== Grounds ==
The shrine grounds include:

* Main Shrine Hall (Haiden, Heiden, Honden)
* {{ill|Mountain Shrine|ja|山神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yama Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11470798}} for child blessings
* {{ill|Tenjinsha|ja|天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11443279}} for academic success

* {{nihongo|'''Mikumari-sha'''|水分神}} for water blessings
* A Frog-shaped Stone Shrine for safe travels and recoveries
* Remains of Jōmon-period ritual sites
